subject: chemistry
title: Acids & Bases Adventure 3: Buffers and titration curves
welcome_lead: Today you'll build buffers and read titration curves with Henderson-Hasselbalch.
meta_desc: Chemistry — buffer solutions, Henderson-Hasselbalch, titration curves, indicators.
final_note: You learned buffers resist pH change (weak acid + conjugate base); Henderson-Hasselbalch: pH = pKa + log([A⁻]/[HA]); titration curves identify equivalence and pKa.

concepts.def: Resists pH change on adding acid/base

walkthroughs.body_html:
A buffer is a weak acid + its conjugate base (e.g. CH₃COOH + CH₃COONa).

Add H⁺ → A⁻ + H⁺ → HA (absorbed).
Add OH⁻ → HA + OH⁻ → A⁻ + H₂O.

pH barely changes — perfect for blood (HCO₃⁻ / H₂CO₃ keeps blood at pH 7.4).

pH = pKa + log([A⁻] / [HA])

If [A⁻] = [HA] → pH = pKa.

Example: buffer with 0.20 M CH₃COOH + 0.10 M CH₃COO⁻ (pKa = 4.76).
pH = 4.76 + log(0.10/0.20) = 4.76 - 0.30 = 4.46.

Strong acid + strong base: vertical jump pH 3→11 around equivalence at pH 7.

Weak acid + strong base: equivalence above 7; pH at half-equivalence = pKa. Buffer region.

Indicators must change colour in vertical region:
- Methyl orange (3.1-4.4): SA-WB.
- Phenolphthalein (8.3-10): WA-SB.
- Both work for SA-SB.

mcqs.q: At half-equivalence point of a weak acid titration:
Why does the colour of a transition metal complex change when ligands are exchanged?
options: Different ligands cause different amounts of d-orbital splitting, so different wavelengths of light are absorbed.
The new concentration is 2 mol/dm^3 because adding water makes the solution stronger.
The colour changes because the new ligand is itself coloured.
The colour changes because the metal ion itself changes oxidation state.

mcqs.q: If 50 cm^3 of a 1 mol/dm^3 solution is diluted to 100 cm^3, what is the new concentration?
options: Atoms across a period have more shells, pulling electrons closer.
The new concentration is 0.05 mol/dm^3 because you doubled the volume so you halve the concentration once and shift the decimal too.
0.5 mol/dm^3 — the moles stay the same but the volume doubled.
The new concentration is 2 mol/dm^3 because adding water makes the solution stronger.

mcqs.q: Why does first ionisation energy generally increase across a period?
options: The colour changes because the new ligand is itself coloured.
Nuclear charge increases while shielding stays roughly constant, so electrons are held more tightly.
Atoms get bigger across a period, making electrons easier to add but harder to remove.
Atoms across a period have more shells, pulling electrons closer.
